tagline: Maps of your market, drawn before you commit a budget to it
intro: We map markets for companies about to enter, expand or reposition: who already sells there, where the buyers are, and which ground nobody has claimed yet. Every map comes with the sources behind it.
audience: Strategy, product and expansion teams at Canadian and US B2B companies moving into a new province, state, vertical or price tier, and the investors backing them.
pricing_note: A fixed fee per map, quoted after a free scoping call. Larger studies are split into stages, and you can stop after any stage and keep what we have drawn.

services.title: Market maps
services.description: Every company selling into your space, placed by price and focus on one map, so the crowded ground and the empty ground are plain to see.

services.title: Competitor teardowns
services.description: A close survey of your five nearest rivals: their pricing, packaging, sales process and hiring, written up the same way so you can compare them line by line.

services.title: Customer interviews
services.description: Conversations with buyers in the segment you are eyeing, to learn what they use today, what annoys them and what would make them switch.

services.title: Market sizing
services.description: How many buyers there are, what they spend and how much of that you could realistically reach in your first three years, with the working shown.

process.title: Draw the whole market
process.description: We list everyone who sells to your buyers and place them on one map, from desk research, filings, pricing pages and a handful of expert calls.

process.title: Survey one segment
process.description: Together we pick the part of the map that matters most, then go deep on it with teardowns and pricing analysis.

process.title: Talk to the buyers
process.description: Interviews with the people who would buy from you, so the final map shows not just where the gap is but whether anyone wants it filled.

proof.text: The map showed us an empty corner of the market we had walked past for two years.
proof.source: Vice president of strategy, a Toronto logistics software firm (sample)

proof.text: Their teardowns are now the first thing our sales team reads before a competitive deal.
proof.source: Head of sales, a Calgary energy services company (sample)

proof.text: We stopped after stage one, and it was still worth every dollar.
